_comment: Findings the jsdom COMPONENT supplement found that the browser screen sweep could not.
Single source of truth, deliberately: `a11y.components.test.tsx` imports this file and asserts
each entry against what axe actually reports, so a declaration here cannot drift from reality;
and `tools/write-accessibility-report.mjs` reads it so the review artifact renders these
findings without anyone hand-typing a finding into a generated report.
Numbered S1..Sn to keep them distinct from the browser sweep's A1..An and axe's N1..Nn.
Commit 2 records. Commit 3 fixes and deletes the entry.

findings.help: Required ARIA attributes must be provided
findings.detail: role="meter" is declared with aria-label and aria-valuetext but WITHOUT the required aria-valuenow, so assistive technology is given a meter with no current value.
findings.whyTheBrowserSweepMissedIt: Nothing in src/ renders RatioBar. It is exported from components.tsx and has no call site, so no screen can exhibit the defect and no screen-level audit could ever have found it. A test asserts that call-site absence, so if a screen starts using it this finding becomes user-facing and must appear in the browser baseline too.
findings.commit3Options: Add aria-valuenow (the projected ratio is already available), or delete the unused component. Either way the characterisation test in a11y.components.test.tsx must be updated, which is the intended pressure.
